bounds.rationale: Two frames give at least one retire-then-restart cycle, so the budget-monotone property and the per-frame reset of the allocation accounting are both exercised.
Java's fixed control-payload limit, used verbatim rather than a scaled-down stand-in, so the gate comparisons run against the real constant.
The port's default max_frame_payload_bytes (rust/ws-core/src/config.rs LimitField::MaxFramePayloadBytes), used verbatim.

One bit per octet on the mask track. XOR acts independently per bit position, so the reduced domain is exact for the involution and key-alignment properties; the module's ASSUME separately checks the full two-bit XOR table exhaustively.
Longer than the four-octet mask key, so the key index wraps and a misalignment mutation is detectable.

findings.statement: The shipped port checks the 125-octet control-payload limit twice: it rejects any control frame whose length marker is >= 126 at header byte 2, and it separately compares the decoded payload length against 125 at the length site. The second comparison is UNREACHABLE, because a control frame that survives the first gate has an inline marker and therefore a length of at most 125. TLC confirms this mechanically: ControlOverLimitRejectedAtBaseHeader holds, so every over-limit control frame is rejected at consumed offset 2. The shipped Java gate has the same shape (drafts/Draft_6455.java:617-620 throws for PING/PONG/CLOSING as soon as the >125 escape is entered, before the extended length bytes are read), so the port's second comparison is defensive depth and matches the fidelity authority. No change is required.

The checker contradicted the author. The first executed TLC run of this model (same attempt, same sandbox, same 3,618-state space) showed that the declared key-index mutation SURVIVED the original MaskRoundTrip invariant with exit 0 and no error: XOR with any fixed index function is an involution, so a round-trip-only check is blind to key ALIGNMENT and the invariant was partially vacuous, with a wrong falsification note. The fix is in the MODEL, not the port: the mask equation is now restated independently as MaskEquationReference and the invariant checks the transform against it. The same mutation is now killed with exit 12 (receipt tlc-mutant-frame-mask.out). The port's mask function was never in question; the defect was in the check.

honesty_notes: Claim ceiling proved-model, full stop. This run establishes properties of an ABSTRACTION of the shipped decoder and nothing about production Rust without a reviewed composition/refinement link. It is not a proof about the shipped framing module.

The model is bounded. MaxFrames = 2 and the four length classes mean the checked results hold only for behaviors inside those bounds; nothing is claimed beyond them, and lengths strictly between the class representatives are not enumerated.

OWNER_ATTESTED_NOT_INDEPENDENT: one session authored the model, the invariants, the falsification notes, and this record, and ran the checker. The correlated-failure risk is real -- a shared blind spot between a model and its own checks is exactly what finding.frame.mask-round-trip-was-vacuous exhibited, and it surfaced only because a mutation was actually EXECUTED rather than assumed to kill.

Non-vacuity is partial, stated precisely: four of the ten invariants (MaskRoundTrip, AllocationRespectsHeaderGate, OverCapRejectedAtLengthSite) plus one property (FramesAlwaysResolve) have an EXECUTED seeded-defect kill in this attempt -- three invariants and one property, four kills total. The remaining seven invariants and the FrameBudgetMonotone property carry declared falsification notes that were NOT executed here; their non-vacuity is asserted, not machine-confirmed.

The authorization for this attempt extends a standing owner decision whose literal text authorized one attempt, already consumed by us007-sbx-output-live-0125. That extension is disclosed in the attempt's own authorization record and is the owner's to ratify or reject.

The two-track structure means the decode obligations and the mask obligations were checked in the SAME run but over DISJOINT state spaces. Nothing here checks their composition -- that an accepted masked frame's payload is the one that gets unmasked -- and no such claim is made.
